checks.covers: Assignment of the ECB cipher mode on a symmetric algorithm object
checks.misses: Modes chosen through a variable or configuration; padding schemes; other libraries

checks.covers: Construction of an AES cipher in ECB mode through the openssl crate
checks.misses: ECB through crates other than openssl; padding schemes such as PKCS#1 v1.5

checks.covers: Cipher.getInstance with a string literal naming AES in ECB mode
checks.misses: Cipher names built at run time or read from configuration; weak padding such as RSA PKCS#1 v1.5

checks.covers: openssl_encrypt called with a cipher name that contains ecb
checks.misses: Cipher names held in variables or constants; weak padding schemes

entries.why: These four rules flag the one insecure block mode the requirement names, ECB, at the literal call sites each models; the JavaScript, Python and Go rules do not look for ECB and are not named.

checks.misses: Algorithms chosen through variables; a cipher outside the weak list that is still not approved; libraries other than node crypto

entries.why: Each rule flags a cipher on a short list of well-known broken algorithms, which is use of a cipher outside the approved set; it cannot show that every cipher in use is approved.

checks.covers: md5 or sha1 applied to an argument whose name suggests a password
checks.misses: Only password-like arguments are flagged, so MD5 or SHA-1 used for signatures, HMAC or key derivation is missed

entries.why: MD5 and SHA-1 are the disallowed hash functions the requirement names, and each rule flags their use at the call sites it models; it does not tell a cryptographic use from a checksum.

checks.covers: md5 or sha1 applied to an argument whose name suggests a password
checks.misses: Passwords hashed through other fast hashes, or with no hash at all; password-like names the pattern does not match; the cost settings of a good password hash; every other language

entries.why: For PHP the rule flags a password passed to MD5 or SHA-1, a storage choice the requirement rules out; it says nothing about the cost settings of an approved function.
